summary: We built LEOVEX to investigate the unique aeolian megaripples at Waw an Namus in southern Libya and evaluate them as a terrestrial analog for Transverse Aeolian Ridges (TARs) on Mars. Using multi-spectral satellite imagery and spatial data analysis, our project bridges Earth observation with planetary science, providing valuable geomorphological insights to support future space exploration and rover mobility planning.
details: LEOVEX is an integrated planetary analog research project focused on Waw an Namus, Libya. We developed an interactive Mission Control web dashboard, conducted spatial analysis using Python, and processed Sentinel-2 and HiRISE satellite datasets. Our project delivers a comprehensive morphometric feature inventory comparing Earth megaripples with Martian TARs, offering high scientific value, open-access transparency, and clean minimalist design.
